newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil firmer, supply tight, delays seen.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil firmer, supply tight, delays seen.

text.p: NWE spot gas oil prices were $2-3 a tonne firmer on Monday with tighter Rotterdam supplies strengthening premiums to firmer benchmark IPE gas oil futures.
However, brokers said outright trade was thin with a strong dollar versus the Deutschmark keeping demand from the key German market quiet.
"The Germans are buying cheaper oil inland" one broker said.
A backlog of barges waiting to load at the jointly owned BP, Texaco Nerefco refinery in Rotterdam was also seen causing short-term supply problems, traders said.
"The problem is that everybody wants to load on the 16th and in order to avoid demurrage costs the refiners have put some nominations for the 16th back to the 18th," one trader said.
Balance of July heating oil barges for Rotterdam refinery lifting were trading and valued around $1.75 a tonne over the August gas oil contract with storage material around 50 cents cheaper.
Diesel barges were offered around August +$5.50 in Rotterdam with Flushing and Antwerp loadings around 50 cents cheaper buyers fro both were scarce.
Cargoes were also slightly firmer as a knock-on effect of the tighter Rotterdam market. O.2 sulphur cargoes were valued around August IPE +$1.75-$2 a tonne cif NWE after trade at +$1.75 on Friday.
Diesel talked around August IPE +$4.50/+$5 after trading at $4.75 cif NWE for delivery by July 20th on Friday.
